- access-new-relic-logs: Use when you or the user wants to investigate logs for app.
- access-outlook-business-email: Use when you or the user wants to read, search, triage, or reason about a Microsoft 365 business mailbox, or draft a reply or new email for the user to review and send. This skill never sends — it only creates drafts.
- access-xero-for-px: Access Pharmacy-Xpress Xero data through the official Custom Connection and confirmed logged-in web routes. Use for Xero reads, writes, reports, bank statement lines, reconciliation, VAT, forecasts, analytics, budgets, files, or assets.
- anvil-yaml: Update Anvil app manifest files in `anvil.yaml`, including services, app metadata, and `db_schema`, using the Anvil YAML type reference available to this agent and `anvil --json validate`.
- brand-guidelines: Applies Anthropic's official brand colors and typography to any sort of artifact that may benefit from having Anthropic's look-and-feel. Use it when brand colors or style guidelines, visual formatting, or company design standards apply.
- call-another-llm: Call Codex CLI or Claude Code CLI with a prompt and save the response to tmp/llm-responses/. Use when you need a second opinion, want to offload a subtask, or compare answers across LLMs.
- canvas-design: Create beautiful visual art in .png and .pdf documents using design philosophy. You should use this skill when the user asks to create a poster, piece of art, design, or other static piece. Create original visual designs, never copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations.
- chatgpt-pro-browser-query: Query ChatGPT through the user's already signed-in browser session while proving ChatGPT Pro and Extended Pro are active before sending. Use this whenever the user asks an agent to ask ChatGPT, use ChatGPT Pro, compare with ChatGPT, query the ChatGPT web app, or get a second opinion specifically from their ChatGPT subscription instead of the API.
- chrome-control: Shared Chrome DevTools control bridge that owns the single CDP connection so multiple Chrome-using skills run from one Chrome "Allow control" approval. Use as STEP 1 of any skill that drives the user's Chrome (ChatGPT browser query, ChatGPT image generation, future browser-driving skills).
- chrome-devtools-cli: Use this skill to write shell scripts or run shell commands to automate tasks in the browser or otherwise use Chrome DevTools via CLI.
- claude-epic-pr-review: Token-intensive, maximal review of a large pull request or branch. Runs three parallel review streams — a 5-agent Codex xhigh swarm with overlapping coverage, an adversarial multi-agent epic-review workflow, and a fork that validates every existing PR comment after checks pass — then consolidates all findings, auto-fixes valid code bugs in parallel while asking the user about UX / DB-schema / new-file decisions, runs /code-review max + /simplify max, and replaces the PR. Use for large, high-risk, or cross-cutting changes when an exhaustive, deliberately expensive review is wanted.
- claude-team-review-plan-implementation: Launch a large team of agents (Codex, Opus teammates) to line-by-line compare a reference plan against its implementation across multiple repos, extract deviations, validate, fix, verify, triage design decisions with the user, simplify, and create PRs. Accepts a reference file name as its argument.
- client-forms: Create, inspect, edit, style, validate, and convert Anvil client Forms under `client_code`, including Form Python, HTML templates, event wiring, Data Bindings, RepeatingPanel item templates, reusable Forms, theme CSS, and legacy YAML templates.
- client-modules: Edit Anvil client code Python modules under `client_code` that are not form definitions, without touching read-only dependencies or form templates.
- codex-image-generation: Generate or edit images through Codex CLI's built-in image_gen tool, driven headlessly via `codex exec` on the user's ChatGPT subscription (no OPENAI_API_KEY, no browser). Use whenever the user asks an agent to "generate an image", "make an image with Codex/ChatGPT", edit an existing image, produce icons/mock-ups/hero art/social assets, or create transparent-background PNGs. Supports single generate, multi-prompt batch, image editing, and chroma-key transparency. Final images are written to `<cwd>/tmp/codex-image-generation` by default (override with `--output-dir`).
- data-models: Design idiomatic Anvil data models and client/server data flow for new apps, CRUD workflows, Data Tables, model classes, buffering, drafts, Data Bindings, and server methods. Use before choosing an architecture for persisted domain data, when the user asks about Anvil models/model classes, or when deciding whether to pass rows, model objects, dicts, or server-callable payloads.
- doc-coauthoring: Guide users through a structured workflow for co-authoring documentation. Use when user wants to write documentation, proposals, technical specs, decision docs, or similar structured content. This workflow helps users efficiently transfer context, refine content through iteration, and verify the doc works for readers. Trigger when user mentions writing docs, creating proposals, drafting specs, or similar documentation tasks.
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
- frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- gws-calendar: Google Calendar: Manage calendars and events.
- gws-docs: Read and write Google Docs.
- gws-drive: Google Drive: Manage files, folders, and shared drives.
- gws-gmail: Gmail: Send, read, and manage email.
- gws-keep: Manage Google Keep notes.
- gws-people: Google People: Manage contacts and profiles.
- gws-script: Manage Google Apps Script projects.
- gws-shared: gws CLI: Shared patterns for authentication, global flags, and output formatting.
- gws-sheets: Google Sheets: Read and write spreadsheets.
- gws-slides: Google Slides: Read and write presentations.
- gws-tasks: Google Tasks: Manage task lists and tasks.
- implement-good-test-patterns: Use datasette-enrichments as a testing reference and imitate its pytest patterns when adding or restructuring tests. Use when writing tests, improving test structure, or aligning a Python project with good integration-style pytest patterns.
- initiate-smoke-tests: Interactive smoke-test runner. Reset the Neon test branch, patch in the fixtures the tests need, then walk the user through each UI smoke test one at a time via AskUser — the question names the exact app, care home, patient(s), med(s), and action. Forks (`subagent_type "fork"`, full context) do every DB sanity check, doc status update, and bug fix. Use when the user says "initiate smoke tests", "let's run the smoke tests", "start/resume smoke testing", or wants to execute a smoke-test doc against the test environment.
- mailshot-carehomes: Use when you or the user wants to send a single bulk announcement (mailshot) to every care-home portal contact - e.g. a new branding link, a portal change, a service notice. Gathers all care-home recipient emails from the Anvil carehome_portal_users table and the Neon "PX" script-copy table, then drafts ONE email (FROM team@, CC stacey@, BCC every care-home contact + zoe@/paresh@/mandeep@) via the access-outlook-business-email skill. Never sends - it only creates a draft for the user to review and send.
- manage-m365-tenant: Use when you or the user wants to administer the Microsoft 365 tenancy — users, groups, licenses, roles, domains, devices, policies, security alerts, audit logs, SharePoint sites, Teams, and usage reports. Full read/write control via Microsoft Graph.
- mk-feature-plan-mode: Plan and prototype a feature before implementation. Map the codebase, grill decisions, persist domain knowledge through /domain-modeling, and invoke /prototype for every UI change or material behaviour uncertainty. Reviewers iterate the plan and prototype together until the user approves the experience. Then write and open a self-contained feature_plan_<feature>.html, plus a test-verified migration.py only for non-additive schema changes. Use for "feature plan mode", "plan this feature", "design doc for ...", or any reviewable UX/architecture plan.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- performance-metrics-from-new-relic: Use when you or the user wants frontend performance metrics from New Relic, including Largest Contentful Paint, Interaction to Next Paint, Cumulative Layout Shift, poor distributions, and worst URLs or sessions.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.

Use when the user wants existing PR comments triaged before deciding what to fix.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- quick-smoke-tests: Generate an ordered, dependency-aware list of UI smoke tests for the work just completed in this session. Walk the user through every test using the AskUser tool — one question per test with all details embedded in the question — then validate each reported result against the database. Use when the user says "smoke test what we just did", "let's quickly verify the changes in the UI", or similar after implementation work.
- server-code: Edit Anvil server code Python modules under `server_code`, including server-callable functions, background logic, and server packages, while keeping changes isolated to the app workspace.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

- sync-mcps: Sync canonical MCP server manifests into Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Cursor config files. Use when you need to add, remove, or update an MCP across all agents from one source of truth, or to diff installed MCP configs against canon.
- taste: Reverse-engineer the design taste of any website. Use whenever the user wants to extract a site's design system, study a competitor's visual language, port an aesthetic to a new project, or generate design guidance for an AI coding agent. Triggers on '/taste <url>', 'analyze the design of X', 'what makes X's site good', 'extract design tokens from X', 'give me X's design DNA', 'build something in the style of X', 'I want my app to feel like X'. - theme-factory: Toolkit for styling artifacts with a theme. These artifacts can be slides, docs, reportings, HTML landing pages, etc. There are 10 pre-set themes with colors/fonts that you can apply to any artifact that has been creating, or can generate a new theme on-the-fly.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). 480	def _read_payload():
481	    candidates = []
482	    try:
483	        # (HOOK-STDIN-UTF8) UTF-8-decode the raw bytes: Windows text-mode
484	        # stdin decodes cp1252 and mojibakes non-ASCII payload chars. Captured
485	        # live 2026-07-28: a teammate background_tasks description's em-dash
486	        # (U+2014, 3 UTF-8 bytes) arrived as 3 cp1252 chars, so the
487	        # (TEAM-ENTRY-MATCH) prefix match against the correctly-decoded
488	        # transcript prompt failed on that one entry forever -> the lead
489	        # terminal's dot latched yellow with zero agents running. Strict
490	        # decode first (payloads are harness-emitted JSON, always valid
491	        # UTF-8); on the never-expected failure, log loud and fall back to
492	        # replacement decoding so the hook still POSTs the lifecycle event.
493	        data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
494	        try:
495	            raw = data.decode("utf-8")
496	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
497	            try:
498	                _log({
499	                    "action": "payload-decode-error",
500	                    "error": str(exc),
501	                    "stdinBytes": len(data),
502	                })
503	            except Exception:
504	                pass
505	            raw = data.decode("utf-8", "replace")
506	        if raw:
507	            candidates.append(raw)
508	    except (OSError, ValueError):
509	        pass
510	    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
511	        candidates.append(sys.argv[1])
512	    for src in candidates:
513	        try:
514	            parsed = json.loads(src)
515	        except (ValueError, TypeError):
516	            continue
517	        if isinstance(parsed, dict):
518	            return parsed
519	    return {}

745	def _pid_alive(pid):
746	    # NOTE: this is the CODEX-job liveness probe. A SECOND, deliberately
747	    # different probe -- _manifest_pid_alive -- lives further down for host
748	    # manifests. They are not interchangeable and must never be merged: this
749	    # one fails CLOSED-ish toward "still active" (an uncertain pid keeps the
750	    # dot moving), while the manifest probe fails OPEN toward "keep the
751	    # candidate" and treats access-denied as alive. This one additionally
752	    # coerces the pid with int(), rejects pid <= 0, and confirms the exit code
753	    # is STILL_ACTIVE, because a codex record can carry a junk pid and a
754	    # not-yet-reaped handle must not read as running.
755	    #
756	    # (BF) Best-effort process-liveness, used to reject a STALE codex job file
757	    # (a worker hard-killed before it could write its terminal status leaves a
758	    # stale running record that the companion's cwd-scoped SessionEnd cleanup
759	    # may never prune — without this it would pin a false dot for the rest of
760	    # the Claude session). On ANY uncertainty return True (the SAFE direction:
761	    # keep showing activity rather than risk a false green). Never raises.
762	    try:
763	        pid = int(pid)
764	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
765	        return True  # no / non-int pid -> cannot disprove -> assume active
766	    if pid <= 0:
767	        return True
768	    try:
769	        if os.name == "nt":
770	            import ctypes
771	            PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION = 0x1000
772	            STILL_ACTIVE = 259
773	            kernel32 = ctypes.windll.kernel32
774	            handle = kernel32.OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, False, pid)
775	            if not handle:
776	                return False  # no such process (own-user worker -> not access-denied)
777	            try:
778	                code = ctypes.c_ulong()
779	                if kernel32.GetExitCodeProcess(handle, ctypes.byref(code)):
780	                    return code.value == STILL_ACTIVE
781	                return True
782	            finally:
783	                kernel32.CloseHandle(handle)
784	        try:
785	            os.kill(pid, 0)
786	            return True
787	        except ProcessLookupError:
788	            return False
789	        except PermissionError:
790	            return True  # exists, owned by someone else
791	    except Exception:
792	        return True
793	    return True

809	def _codex_job_active(session_id, detail_out=None, skipped_out=None):
810	    # (BF codex-companion parity) The codex plugin dispatches review/task work
811	    # to a DETACHED worker process that is invisible to Claude Code's
812	    # Stop-payload background_tasks[], so neither (BA) nor (TEAM-YELLOW) alone
813	    # surfaces it (terminal greens to idle while codex still runs). The
814	    # companion records each job as a JSON file with a status and the Claude
815	    # session_id (its CODEX_COMPANION_SESSION_ID is the SessionStart session_id
816	    # — the SAME id this hook receives). So an ACTIVE codex job for THIS
817	    # session is delegated agent work -> the dot stays on, like a teammate.
818	    # We do NOT inherit the codex plugin's CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA (it is
819	    # per-plugin), so glob the known on-disk job stores instead. "Active"
820	    # defers to the plugin's own definition (queued|running) AND requires the
821	    # job's worker pid to still be alive (_pid_alive). A transient mid-write
822	    # JSON read failure is skipped (-> a one-event missed hold that
823	    # self-corrects on the next turn-end: the SAFE direction). Bounded:
824	    # evaluated only at a real turn/subagent end (see _decide_event_type),
825	    # short-circuits on first match. Never raises.
826	    # detail_out (optional list): when provided, the holding job's
827	    # "<jobfile> pid=<pid> mtime_age=<s>s" is appended on a positive match, so
828	    # the always-on decision log can name exactly what held the dot.
829	    # skipped_out (optional list): when provided, a pid-ALIVE 'running' record
830	    # DISCARDED by the 6h staleness cap appends its
831	    # "<jobfile> pid=<pid> pid_alive=true mtime_age=<s>s cap=21600s" here. This
832	    # is the EXACT shape of the original stuck-yellow incident (a reused-pid
833	    # record aged past the cap) AND of a false-green of a genuinely long codex
834	    # job (see the cap caveat below). Without it the GREEN reason reads "no
835	    # active holds" and a reader cannot tell a stale/long codex record was
836	    # silently dropped vs there genuinely being nothing running.
837	    #
838	    # CAP CAVEAT (review findings #1/#4): the 6h cap assumes the codex-companion
839	    # worker touches its job JSON at least every <6h while alive. The producer
840	    # (the external openai-codex plugin's tracked-jobs.mjs) only rewrites the
841	    # JSON on phase/threadId/turnId CHANGE — there is NO periodic heartbeat — so
842	    # a legitimate job that stays in one phase for >6h (a long shell/model/
843	    # network wait) ages past the cap and is skipped here, dropping yellow to
844	    # green while still running. The cap is therefore a pid-REUSE heuristic, not
845	    # a liveness boundary; it deliberately self-corrects toward GREEN (the
846	    # file's documented SAFE direction) rather than risk a permanent stuck
847	    # yellow. The skipped_out logging above makes any such premature-green
848	    # immediately auditable in dot-decisions.log. A non-decaying liveness signal
849	    # (pid start-time/cmdline identity, or a companion-emitted heartbeat) would
850	    # remove the trade-off but lives in the external plugin / needs cross-platform
851	    # process introspection, so it is intentionally NOT done here.
852	    if not session_id:
853	        return False
854	    try:
855	        home = pathlib.Path.home()
856	        roots = [(home / ".claude" / "plugins" / "data", "codex*/state/*/jobs/*.json")]
857	        try:
858	            import tempfile
859	            roots.append((pathlib.Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "codex-companion", "*/jobs/*.json"))
860	        except Exception:
861	            pass
862	        active = ("queued", "running")
863	        for root, pattern in roots:
864	            try:
865	                for jf in root.glob(pattern):
866	                    # (R1 review) retry once on a parse failure: the worker
867	                    # rewrites the job JSON in place, so a read can land
868	                    # mid-write; skipping outright at the exact Stop moment
869	                    # would false-GREEN a still-running job.
870	                    rec = None
871	                    for _ in range(2):
872	                        try:
873	                            with open(jf, "r", encoding="utf-8") as h:
874	                                rec = json.load(h)
875	                            break
876	                        except Exception:
877	                            rec = None
878	                    if not isinstance(rec, dict):
879	                        continue
880	                    if rec.get("sessionId") != session_id:
881	                        continue
882	                    if (rec.get("status") or "") not in active:
883	                        continue
884	                    pid = rec.get("pid")
885	                    try:
886	                        int(pid)
887	                        has_pid = True
888	                    except (TypeError, ValueError):
889	                        has_pid = False
890	                    if has_pid:
891	                        # (pid-reuse guard) A 'running' record with a live pid is
892	                        # NOT trusted on its own: pids are recycled by the OS, so a
893	                        # long-dead worker's pid can read alive on an UNRELATED
894	                        # process and pin yellow forever (live incident: a 15-day-old
895	                        # 'running' record whose reused pid passed _pid_alive held the
896	                        # dot working for hours while idle). Require the job JSON to
897	                        # have been touched within 6h (the worker rewrites it as it
898	                        # progresses); an older record is stale -> skip it.
899	                        if _pid_alive(pid):
900	                            try:
901	                                import time
902	                                age = time.time() - jf.stat().st_mtime
903	                                if age < 21600:
904	                                    if detail_out is not None:
905	                                        detail_out.append(
906	                                            str(jf) + " pid=" + str(pid)
907	                                            + " mtime_age=" + str(int(age)) + "s"
908	                                        )
909	                                    return True
910	                                # pid alive but record aged past the cap: the
911	                                # exact incident (reused-pid stale record) OR a
912	                                # real >6h-in-one-phase job. Record the skip so
913	                                # the GREEN reason can name it (review #2).
914	                                if skipped_out is not None:
915	                                    skipped_out.append(
916	                                        str(jf) + " pid=" + str(pid)
917	                                        + " pid_alive=true mtime_age=" + str(int(age))
918	                                        + "s cap=21600s"
919	                                    )
920	                            except Exception:
921	                                if detail_out is not None:
922	                                    detail_out.append(str(jf) + " pid=" + str(pid) + " mtime_age=?")
923	                                return True
924	                        continue
925	                    # (R1 review) pid-less active record: a job written as
926	                    # queued whose worker never spawned would otherwise hold
927	                    # yellow for the REST of the session. Age-gate it — fresh
928	                    # (<10 min) counts as active (spawn in progress), older is
929	                    # stale and skipped.
930	                    try:
931	                        import time
932	                        age = time.time() - jf.stat().st_mtime
933	                        if age < 600:
934	                            if detail_out is not None:
935	                                detail_out.append(
936	                                    str(jf) + " pid=none mtime_age=" + str(int(age)) + "s"
937	                                )
938	                            return True
939	                    except Exception:
940	                        if detail_out is not None:
941	                            detail_out.append(str(jf) + " pid=none mtime_age=?")
942	                        return True  # cannot disprove -> active (safe)
943	            except Exception:
944	                continue
945	        return False
946	    except Exception:
947	        return False

950	# (MARKER-RECONCILE) statuses that mean a background_tasks[] entry is over.
951	# Shared by _split_background and _running_bg_ids so the yellow/blue split and

987	    if not isinstance(bg_tasks, list):

990	    has_agent = False
991	    has_shell = False

1084	def _team_scan_text(state, text):
1085	    # Update the name -> "active"|"idle" ledger from one transcript text blob.
1086	    # String scanning only (NO regex): this file is a TS template literal, and
1087	    # single backslashes in regex escapes would be silently swallowed.
1088	    # (TEAM-ENTRY-MATCH) A duplicate teammate name is delivered with a
1089	    # " [hash]" suffix in its messages while the spawn recorded the base name;
1090	    # mirror every suffixed update onto the base key so the base key tracks
1091	    # the LATEST same-named instance instead of latching a stale idle.
1092	    # Accepted narrow risk (review 2026-07-22): same name + identical prompt
1093	    # head + the OLD instance silently working when the new one idles can
1094	    # false-green the old entry until its next message re-actives the base.
1095	    #
1096	    # (TEAM-ENTRY-BIND) Scanned in DOCUMENT ORDER across BOTH tag kinds. The
1097	    # original two-pass scan ran every teammate-message first and every
1098	    # agent-message second, so within one delivered blob an agent-message always
1099	    # won regardless of position: a teammate that reported (agent-message) and
1100	    # then idled (idle_notification teammate-message) in the same blob latched
1101	    # "active" forever, which is one of the ways the all-idle predicate became
1102	    # unsatisfiable. Later evidence must win, so the later TAG must win.
1103	    tag = '<teammate-message teammate_id="'
1104	    tag2 = '<agent-message from="'
1105	    pos = 0
1106	    while True:
1107	        i = text.find(tag, pos)
1108	        a = text.find(tag2, pos)
1109	        if i < 0 and a < 0:
1110	            break
1111	        if a < 0 or (i >= 0 and i < a):
1112	            j = i + len(tag)
1113	            k = text.find('"', j)
1114	            if k < 0:
1115	                break
1116	            name = text[j:k]
1117	            end = text.find("</teammate-message>", k)
1118	            body = text[k:end] if end > 0 else text[k:]
1119	            _team_set_state(
1120	                state, name, "idle" if '"idle_notification"' in body else "active"
1121	            )
1122	            pos = k
1123	        else:
1124	            b = a + len(tag2)
1125	            c = text.find('"', b)
1126	            if c < 0:
1127	                break
1128	            _team_set_state(state, text[b:c], "active")
1129	            pos = c

1306	def _team_cache_lock(cache_file):
1307	    # Serialize the whole read/scan/bind/replace transaction. os.replace makes
1308	    # one write atomic but cannot stop an older overlapping process from
1309	    # replacing a newer cache afterward. The one-byte lock works on Windows
1310	    # and POSIX, waits at most two seconds, and returns None on every acquisition
1311	    # error so uncertain rows stay yellow rather than running unlocked.
1312	    lock_file = cache_file.with_name(cache_file.name + ".lock")
1313	    handle = None
1314	    try:
1315	        lock_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1316	        handle = open(lock_file, "a+b")
1317	        handle.seek(0, 2)
1318	        if handle.tell() == 0:
1319	            handle.write(b"\\0")
1320	            handle.flush()
1321	        deadline = time.monotonic() + 2.0
1322	        while True:
1323	            try:
1324	                handle.seek(0)
1325	                if os.name == "nt":
1326	                    import msvcrt
1327	                    msvcrt.locking(handle.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1)
1328	                else:
1329	                    import fcntl
1330	                    fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
1331	                return handle
1332	            except OSError as error:
1333	                if error.errno not in (errno.EACCES, errno.EAGAIN, errno.EDEADLK):
1334	                    _log({
1335	                        "action": "teamstate-lock-error",
1336	                        "phase": "acquire",
1337	                        "error": type(error).__name__ + ": " + str(error),
1338	                    })
1339	                    handle.close()
1340	                    return None
1341	                if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
1342	                    handle.close()
1343	                    return None
1344	                time.sleep(0.025)
1345	    except Exception as error:
1346	        _log({
1347	            "action": "teamstate-lock-error",
1348	            "phase": "open",
1349	            "error": type(error).__name__ + ": " + str(error),
1350	        })
1351	        try:
1352	            if handle is not None:
1353	                handle.close()
1354	        except Exception:
1355	            pass
1356	        return None
1357

1359	def _team_cache_unlock(handle):
1360	    ok = True
1361	    try:
1362	        handle.seek(0)
1363	        if os.name == "nt":
1364	            import msvcrt
1365	            msvcrt.locking(handle.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)
1366	        else:
1367	            import fcntl
1368	            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

1373	            "phase": "release",

1375	        })
1376	    try:
1377	        handle.close()
1378	    except Exception as error:

1673	def _team_bind_entries(entry_names, seen_ids, entry_ids, spawns):
1674	    # (TEAM-ENTRY-BIND) Bind each FIRST-SEEN running teammate entry id to the
1675	    # spawn name(s) it appeared alongside, forget bindings for ids that have left
1676	    # the running set, and return the updated (bindings, seen ids).
1677	    #
1678	    # Why this exists: a teammate entry carries ONLY {id, type, status,
1679	    # description}, and the description is the spawn prompt's first ~50 chars.
1680	    # Leads template that preamble (live 2026-08-18: every teammate in a session
1681	    # described as "Repo: C:...worktrees/<uuid>-" — exactly 50 chars of
1682	    # boilerplate), so the (TEAM-ENTRY-MATCH) prefix join maps ONE running entry
1683	    # onto EVERY teammate the session ever spawned. The all-matching-names-idle
1684	    # rule is then unsatisfiable the moment any one of them is stuck "active",
1685	    # and the lead's yellow can never be released: the single running teammate
1686	    # idled at 14:50:35Z, the turn-end Stop fired 6s later with the correct
1687	    # ledger state, and seven unrelated names (three last heard from 19-26h
1688	    # earlier) kept the entry.
1689	    #
1690	    # The entry id is stable for the entry's lifetime and appears nowhere else on
1691	    # disk, so no exact join exists — but an id that has NEVER been listed before
1692	    # and IS listed now was created by the spawns observed in between. That is a
1693	    # causal link, not a string guess. One new id + one new spawn binds exactly;
1694	    # any other shape binds the id to the whole candidate batch, which only
1695	    # narrows the prefix bucket rather than identifying within it (still
1696	    # requiring every candidate idle).
1697	    #
1698	    # Narrowing is what makes a drop EASIER, so every input to it is kept
1699	    # deliberately conservative: only teammate-capable spawn types are
1700	    # candidates, pendings never outlive their run, and an id is bindable only
1701	    # once. A wrong binding CAN still false-green (that is the residual risk of
1702	    # binding at all) — it cannot be waved away by "it only narrows".
1703	    live = set(entry_ids)
1704	    bound = {}
1705	    for k, v in entry_names.items():
1706	        if k in live:
1707	            bound[k] = v
1708	    # An id counts as NEW only the FIRST time it is ever observed. An id that
1709	    # was listed before — bound or not, and whether or not it left the running
1710	    # set in between — was NOT created by the spawns parsed since the previous
1711	    # snapshot, and binding it to them is how live work gets false-greened: the
1712	    # harness re-lists a resumed teammate, and an entry the count guard once
1713	    # declined must not become bindable later just because the guard now
1714	    # passes. Both maps stay bounded: bindings prune to the live set, and the
1715	    # seen list keeps only a tail of the ids that have left it.
1716	    seen = set(seen_ids)
1717	    first_seen_ids = [i for i in entry_ids if i and i not in seen]
1718	    new_ids = [i for i in first_seen_ids if i not in bound]
1719	    # More first-seen entries than observed spawns means at least one of them was
1720	    # created by something other than a lead Agent tool-use (a workflow spawning
1721	    # its own teammate), so no assignment is trustworthy. Count rows already
1722	    # exact-bound above too: one spawn cannot be spent once by exact matching and
1723	    # again by this legacy prompt binder. Leave residual rows unbound so the
1724	    # broader prompt bucket keeps uncertain work yellow.
1725	    if new_ids and spawns and len(first_seen_ids) <= len(spawns):
1726	        candidates = list(spawns)
1727	        for i in new_ids:
1728	            bound[i] = candidates
1729	    stale = [i for i in seen_ids if i and i not in live]
1730	    return bound, stale[-192:] + [i for i in entry_ids if i]

1736	):
1737	    # Exact Agent descriptions take precedence. Only a trusted first-seen
1738	    # binding may use them. If no Agent description equals the payload, retain
1739	    # the legacy prompt-prefix behavior (with or without a trailing "...").
1740	    raw_description = str(entry.get("description") or "")
1741	    description = _team_description_key(raw_description)
1742	    prefix = (
1743	        _team_description_key(raw_description[:-3])
1744	        if raw_description.endswith("...")
1745	        else description
1746	    )
1747	    entry_id = str(entry.get("id") or "")
1748	    bound = entry_names.get(entry_id) or []
1749	    exact_names = description_index.get(description, [])
1750	    prompt_matches = []
1751	    description_matches = []
1752	    if exact_names:
1753	        # Exact text without causal trust must stay candidate-free/yellow. Never
1754	        # fall through to legacy prompts: a foreign live row could inherit an
1755	        # idle Agent name and false-ready.
1756	        if entry_id in trusted_ids:
1757	            description_matches = [name for name in exact_names if name in bound]
1758	        candidates = description_matches
1759	    else:
1760	        if len(prefix) >= 12:
1761	            for name, keys in match_keys.items():
1762	                prompts = keys.get("prompts", [])
1763	                # An unbound row may only compare against the name's latest
1764	                # prompt. Old prompt history can belong to finished work and
1765	                # must not make a later foreign row look idle. A causal legacy
1766	                # binding may keep using its older identifying prompt.
1767	                if name not in bound:
1768	                    prompts = prompts[-1:]
1769	                if any(
1770	                    prompt and prompt.startswith(prefix)
1771	                    for prompt in prompts
1772	                ):
1773	                    prompt_matches.append(name)
1774	        narrowed = [name for name in prompt_matches if name in bound]
1775	        candidates = narrowed or prompt_matches
1776	    return (
1777	        prefix,
1778	        prompt_matches,
1779	        description_matches,
1780	        bound,
1781	        candidates,
1782	        entry_id in trusted_ids,
1783	    )

2621	# The PreToolUse:AskUserQuestion payload already carries the WHOLE question:
2622	# tool_use_id, transcript_path, session_id, cwd, tool_input.questions[] (each
2623	# with question / header / multiSelect / options[] -> label + description) and

2625	# tool_name and threw the rest away, so the companion phone/watch had nothing
2626	# to render and no way to discover a question without parsing transcripts.
2627	#
2628	# Everything below is PURELY ADDITIVE. It runs only for AskUserQuestion, it
2629	# never touches _decide_event_type, and on ANY shape surprise it returns None
2630	# and logs -- so a Claude Code payload change can degrade the companion feature
2631	# but can NEVER move a dot. Regressing the dots is not an acceptable trade.

2633	# Style constraints for this embedded template: no backticks (they break the
2634	# esbuild template literal) and no raw backslashes.

2637	def _post_hook(url, body, timeout):
2638	    # Single place the notify POST is issued, so the (COMPANION-CAPTURE)
2639	    # strip-and-retry path sends a byte-identical request to the original.
2640	    #
2641	    # timeout is chosen by the caller and is never above 1.5s: _deliver shrinks
2642	    # it to whatever is left of the total probe budget, so the last attempt of a
2643	    # sweep cannot push the whole sweep past that budget.
2644	    #
2645	    # (DISPOSE-LIMBO) Returns (status, body) for a 2xx and raises
2646	    # urllib.error.HTTPError for anything else. A host-service route that took
2647	    # the event answers 200 -- and so does one that DROPPED it, with an
2648	    # ignored/reason body on purpose -- so the status alone cannot tell a
2649	    # delivered dot from one the host threw away for a terminal it has no row
2650	    # for, which is what a terminal stuck in dispose limbo produces.
2651	    req = urllib.request.Request(
2652	        url,
2653	        data=body,
2654	        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
2655	        method="POST",
2656	    )
2657	    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
2658	        try:
2659	            raw = resp.read(2048).decode("utf-8", "replace")
2660	        except Exception as read_exc:
2661	            raw = "<unreadable response: " + str(read_exc) + ">"
2662	        return resp.status, raw[:500]

2666	# The host-service can restart onto a NEW port at any time. A PTY started
2667	# before that restart keeps the OLD SUPERSET_HOST_AGENT_HOOK_URL in its env
2668	# forever -- a live process's env cannot be rewritten -- so every notify POST
2669	# from that terminal goes to a dead port and the dot silently stops moving,
2670	# INCLUDING the "Start" that clears a red dot once a question is answered.
2671	# Measured on Windows: a dead loopback port takes ~2040ms to refuse, so the
2672	# symptom in the logs is a 1.5s timeout, not ECONNREFUSED.
2673	#
2674	# Fix: treat the env URL as a hint, not the address. Each org's manifest
2675	# (<root>/host/<orgId>/manifest.json) is rewritten with the live endpoint on
2676	# every host start, so it is never stale. This is the same failover the shell
2677	# template already does (packages/agent-setup/templates/notify-hook.template.sh
2678	# :170-214), ported to Python.

2684	def _kernel32():
2685	    # Lazily loaded ONCE per process. Every _manifest_pid_alive call used to
2686	    # re-open kernel32 and re-declare the same two prototypes; the manifest
2687	    # sweep calls it per host, and the load is the expensive part.
2688	    global _KERNEL32
2689	    if _KERNEL32 is None:
2690	        import ctypes
2691	
2692	        lib = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
2693	        lib.OpenProcess.argtypes = [
2694	            ctypes.c_uint32,
2695	            ctypes.c_int,
2696	            ctypes.c_uint32,
2697	        ]
2698	        lib.OpenProcess.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
2699	        lib.CloseHandle.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p]
2700	        _KERNEL32 = lib
2701	    return _KERNEL32

2704	def _manifest_pid_alive(pid):
2705	    # NOTE: distinct from _pid_alive above (the codex-job staleness probe) and
2706	    # deliberately so -- do not collapse the two. That one answers "is this
2707	    # codex worker still working?" and leans toward keeping a dot alive; this
2708	    # one answers "may I POST a payload to the port this manifest names?" and
2709	    # fails OPEN: only a PROVEN-dead pid drops the candidate, and access-denied
2710	    # counts as alive. It also takes the pid as-is (the caller has already
2711	    # type-checked it) instead of coercing.
2712	    #
2713	    # (HOOK-STALE-MANIFEST) Is the host that wrote this manifest still running?
2714	    # A crashed host leaves its manifest behind, and the OS eventually hands
2715	    # that port to an unrelated process -- which would then be POSTed the whole
2716	    # payload, companion question text included. The manifest stamps the
2717	    # writer pid, so a dead pid is a manifest to skip.
2718	    #
2719	    # FAILS OPEN: anything uncertain returns True. Skipping a LIVE host loses a
2720	    # dot; probing a dead one costs a single refused connection.
2721	    #
2722	    # NEVER os.kill(pid, 0) here. On Windows CPython os.kill ignores the signal
2723	    # for everything but the CTRL_*_EVENT constants and calls TerminateProcess,
2724	    # so signal 0 would KILL the process this only means to observe.
2725	    try:
2726	        if sys.platform == "win32":
2727	            import ctypes
2728	
2729	            kernel32 = _kernel32()
2730	            # PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION (0x1000): the weakest right
2731	            # that still proves existence, granted across integrity levels.
2732	            handle = kernel32.OpenProcess(0x1000, 0, int(pid))
2733	            if handle:
2734	                kernel32.CloseHandle(handle)
2735	                return True
2736	            # 87 = ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, which is how Windows reports "no
2737	            # process has that id". Anything else (5 = access denied on a host
2738	            # running elevated or as another user) is a live process this
2739	            # simply cannot open, so it stays a candidate.
2740	            return ctypes.get_last_error() != 87
2741	        os.kill(int(pid), 0)
2742	        return True
2743	    except ProcessLookupError:
2744	        return False
2745	    except Exception:
2746	        return True

2752	def _manifest_candidate_urls(already_queued):
2753	    # Every host-manifest URL worth trying, THIS terminal's org first and the
2754	    # rest by name, minus anything in already_queued and minus manifests whose
2755	    # writer pid is PROVEN dead. Any per-manifest problem skips that manifest
2756	    # with a log line. Never raises.
2757	    #
2758	    # Built at most ONCE per process and memoized: the companion
2759	    # strip-and-retry sweeps the same candidates a second time, and the glob +
2760	    # JSON parse + pid probe is the expensive half of a notify POST. The
2761	    # memoized answer ignores later already_queued arguments, which is safe
2762	    # because the env URL cannot change inside one hook process.
2763	    #
2764	    # SUPERSET_HOME_DIR scopes the MANIFEST GLOB ONLY. Every marker path in this
2765	    # script deliberately keeps using pathlib.Path.home(): the host-service reads
2766	    # those markers at a HARDCODED homedir()
2767	    # (packages/host-service/src/trpc/router/notifications/agent-status-snapshot.ts
2768	    # :133-138), so unifying the two roots would write markers where the host
2769	    # never looks and silently break resync.
2770	    global _MANIFEST_CANDIDATES
2771	    if _MANIFEST_CANDIDATES is not None:
2772	        return _MANIFEST_CANDIDATES
2773	    urls = []
2774	    seen_urls = set(already_queued)
2775	    seen_paths = set()
2776	    try:
2777	        home_dir = os.environ.get("SUPERSET_HOME_DIR")
2778	        if home_dir:
2779	            root = pathlib.Path(home_dir)
2780	        else:
2781	            root = pathlib.Path.home() / ".superset"
2782	        host_dir = root / "host"
2783	        manifest_paths = []
2784	        # This terminal's OWN host first: env.ts:256-257 stamps the org id on
2785	        # every terminal it launches, so the common case probes one URL and
2786	        # stops. Other orgs' hosts answer "ignored":true -- harmless, but slow.
2787	        org_id = os.environ.get("SUPERSET_ORGANIZATION_ID")
2788	        if org_id:
2789	            manifest_paths.append(host_dir / org_id / "manifest.json")
2790	        try:
2791	            manifest_paths.extend(sorted(host_dir.glob("*/manifest.json")))
2792	        except Exception as glob_exc:
2793	            _log({
2794	                "action": "hook-candidate-glob-failed",
2795	                "hostDir": str(host_dir),
2796	                "error": str(glob_exc),
2797	            })
2798	        for manifest_path in manifest_paths:
2799	            # The own-org path is also matched by the glob above. Without this
2800	            # it would be opened, parsed and pid-probed a second time.
2801	            if manifest_path in seen_paths:
2802	                continue
2803	            seen_paths.add(manifest_path)
2804	            try:
2805	                with open(manifest_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
2806	                    manifest = json.loads(handle.read(65536))
2807	                if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
2808	                    raise ValueError("manifest is not an object")
2809	                endpoint = manifest.get("endpoint")
2810	                if not isinstance(endpoint, str) or not endpoint:
2811	                    raise ValueError("manifest has no endpoint string")
2812	                candidate = endpoint.rstrip("/") + "/trpc/notifications.hook"
2813	                # Deduped BEFORE the liveness probe: the common case is the env
2814	                # URL naming this terminal's own host, and a URL already queued
2815	                # is going to be POSTed whatever the probe would answer.
2816	                if candidate in seen_urls:
2817	                    continue
2818	                # (HOOK-STALE-MANIFEST) A crashed host's manifest still names a
2819	                # port some unrelated process may now own. Only skip on PROOF
2820	                # the writer is gone: a missing or unusable pid keeps the entry.
2821	                pid = manifest.get("pid")
2822	                if (
2823	                    isinstance(pid, int)
2824	                    and not isinstance(pid, bool)
2825	                    and pid > 0
2826	                    and not _manifest_pid_alive(pid)
2827	                ):
2828	                    _log({
2829	                        "action": "hook-candidate-manifest-dead-pid",
2830	                        "manifest": str(manifest_path),
2831	                        "pid": pid,
2832	                    })
2833	                    continue
2834	                seen_urls.add(candidate)
2835	                urls.append(candidate)
2836	            except Exception as manifest_exc:
2837	                _log({
2838	                    "action": "hook-candidate-manifest-skipped",
2839	                    "manifest": str(manifest_path),
2840	                    "error": str(manifest_exc),
2841	                })
2842	    except Exception as exc:
2843	        _log({"action": "hook-candidates-failed", "error": str(exc)})
2844	    _MANIFEST_CANDIDATES = urls
2845	    return urls

2903	class _HookUndelivered(RuntimeError):
2904	    # What _deliver raises when nothing accepted the POST.
2905	    #
2906	    # saw_response tells a host that ANSWERED-and-refused -- a 2xx nobody could
2907	    # parse, an outright 4xx from the owning host rejecting the body shape, or
2908	    # a disown sweep carrying an HTTP error -- from a dead port: when NOTHING
2909	    # answered, a stripped-body companion retry cannot answer either, so the
2910	    # caller skips it instead of burning another probe cycle on every
2911	    # candidate.
2912	    def __init__(self, message, saw_response, cause=None):
2913	        super().__init__(message)
2914	        self.saw_response = saw_response
2915	        self.__cause__ = cause
2916	
2917	    @classmethod
2918	    def from_sweep(cls, fallback, saw_response, cause):
2919	        # The underlying transport failure's own str() whenever there is one:
2920	        # the post-error log and the companion retry both surface the message
2921	        # verbatim, and a human needs "HTTP Error 400: Bad Request" there, not
2922	        # "no hook endpoint accepted the event".

2926	def _deliver(candidates, body, tried):
2927	    # POST body to candidates in order until one POSITIVELY accepts it.
2928	    # Returns an _HookOutcome; raises _HookUndelivered on anything else.
2929	    #
2930	    # tried (list, in/out) collects every url actually attempted, in order and
2931	    # deduped across sweeps. candidates is lazy, so this is the only record of
2932	    # what was reached, and the caller logs it.
2933	    #
2934	    # "ignored-everywhere" is a DELIVERED NO-OP and needs at least one
2935	    # candidate to have returned a VALID envelope saying "ignored": true (every
2936	    # reachable host disowns this terminal id; see agent-status-snapshot.ts
2937	    # :41-48 for the ghost-terminal case). A 2xx body that does not parse to
2938	    # that envelope proves the opposite and goes down the raise path, so a
2939	    # foreign server on a recycled port can never be reported as delivery.
2940	    #
2941	    # A disown sweep that ALSO saw an HTTP ERROR status is promoted to a raise
2942	    # here rather than returned: the owning host rejects a bad companion shape
2943	    # with a 400 while a FOREIGN host on the same machine can answer 200
2944	    # "ignored": true in the SAME sweep, so returning a delivered no-op would
2945	    # let the owner's rejection hide behind a stranger and drop the dot with no
2946	    # error anywhere.
2947	    #
2948	    # Bounded by a 4.0s TOTAL probe budget. Each attempt gets
2949	    # min(1.5, remaining), so the per-request cap stays 1.5s AND the whole
2950	    # sweep stays inside the budget -- a machine with several dead hosts
2951	    # cannot stall the agent.
2952	    started = time.monotonic()
2953	    saw_response = False
2954	    last_ignored_body = None
2955	    http_error = None
2956	    last_exc = None
2957	    attempts = 0
2958	    for url in candidates:
2959	        remaining = 4.0 - (time.monotonic() - started)
2960	        if remaining <= 0.0:
2961	            _log({
2962	                "action": "hook-probe-budget-exhausted",
2963	                "elapsedMs": int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000),
2964	                "triedUrls": tried,
2965	            })
2966	            raise _HookUndelivered.from_sweep(
2967	                "hook probe budget exhausted after "
2968	                + str(attempts)
2969	                + " candidate(s)",
2970	                saw_response,
2971	                last_exc,
2972	            )
2973	        attempts += 1
2974	        if url not in tried:
2975	            tried.append(url)
2976	        try:
2977	            status, raw = _post_hook(url, body, min(1.5, remaining))
2978	        except urllib.error.HTTPError as status_exc:
2979	            # A SERVER ANSWERED, with an error status. urllib turns every
2980	            # non-2xx into this exception, which is the only place the owning
2981	            # host schema rejection of a companion payload can land.
2982	            saw_response = True
2983	            last_exc = status_exc
2984	            http_error = (
2985	                "HTTP " + str(getattr(status_exc, "code", "?")) + " from " + url
2986	            )
2987	            _log({
2988	                "action": "hook-candidate-http-error",
2989	                "url": url,
2990	                "status": getattr(status_exc, "code", None),
2991	            })
2992	            continue
2993	        except Exception as exc:
2994	            last_exc = exc
2995	            continue
2996	        saw_response = True
2997	        ignored = _hook_ignored_flag(raw)
2998	        if ignored is False:
2999	            return _HookOutcome("delivered", url, status, raw)
3000	        if ignored is True:
3001	            last_ignored_body = raw
3002	    if last_ignored_body is not None:
3003	        if http_error:
3004	            # The promotion: a disown sweep that also carries an HTTP error.
3005	            # http_error, not the exception's own str(), is the message --
3006	            # it names the host that refused, which the stranger's 200 hides.
3007	            raise _HookUndelivered(http_error, saw_response, last_exc)
3008	        return _HookOutcome("ignored-everywhere", None, None, last_ignored_body)
3009	    raise _HookUndelivered.from_sweep(
3010	        "no hook endpoint accepted the event ("
3011	        + str(attempts)
3012	        + " candidate(s) tried)",
3013	        saw_response,
3014	        last_exc,
3015	    )

import fs from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";

/**
 * Companion to `agent-jsonl-watcher.ts`: installs a tiny portable
 * Python (`uv run python`) SessionStart hook that records the Superset
 * pane/tab/workspace identity alongside each Claude/Codex session id.
 *
 * The watcher reads these mapping files at
 * `~/.superset/session-pane-map/<sessionId>.json` so it can emit
 * `AgentLifecycleEvent`s with a precise paneId — resolving the
 * "multiple terminals in the same cwd" ambiguity that cwd-only
 * resolution can't disambiguate.
 *
 * Why install here (not via agent-setup) — upstream's `agent-wrappers`
 * already manages a bash hook that's broken on Windows; rather than
 * patch the wrapper-registration code, we add an additional managed
 * entry directly. Coexistence is safe: upstream identifies its own
 * entries by `notify.sh` path; we identify ours by the script
 * filename below. The two won't conflict.
 */

const SCRIPT_FILENAME = "superset-pane-map.py";
const SCRIPT_DIR = path.join(os.homedir(), ".superset", "hooks");
const SCRIPT_PATH = path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, SCRIPT_FILENAME);
const CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH = path.join(
	os.homedir(),
	".claude",
	"settings.json",
);
const CODEX_HOOKS_PATH = path.join(os.homedir(), ".codex", "hooks.json");

// Legacy AskUserQuestion deterministic-red hook. RETIRED: superset-notify.py
// now owns the AskUserQuestion red (PreToolUse:AskUserQuestion). Only the
// filename constant survives so mergeNotifyHook can self-heal away any stale
// ask-marker hook a prior build registered; the script body, its writer, its
// command builder, and its merge function were all deleted.
// Still referenced by isAskMarkerHook below, which mergeNotifyHook uses to
// self-heal (drop) any stale ask-marker hook left by a prior build — the
// notify hook now owns the AskUserQuestion red. The ask-marker SCRIPT itself
// is no longer written or registered.
const ASK_MARKER_SCRIPT_FILENAME = "superset-ask-marker.py";

// Claude agent-status hook. A third Python hook POSTs each Claude lifecycle
// event to the host-service so the dots are driven event-driven (no JSONL
// timing heuristics) — reviving what the dead bash `~/.superset/hooks/notify.sh`
// did. Registered (Claude settings.json only) on UserPromptSubmit / Stop /
// SessionEnd / Notification(permission_prompt) and on PreToolUse scoped to
// AskUserQuestion plus an unscoped PostToolUse (a MAIN-LOOP tool completion
// re-asserts working, clearing red after a permission approval or an answered
// question; a tool that ran inside a subagent — payload carries agent_id —
// asserts the red-respecting SubagentActive instead, see (SUBTOOL-RED)).
// The server maps Start→working, Stop→review, PermissionRequest→permission.
// This hook now OWNS Claude working/review/permission (including the
// AskUserQuestion red, so the separate ask-marker hook is no longer registered
// for Claude). Python + `uv run` so it runs on Windows exactly like the
// pane-map hook.
const NOTIFY_SCRIPT_FILENAME = "superset-notify.py";
const NOTIFY_SCRIPT_PATH = path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, NOTIFY_SCRIPT_FILENAME);

/**
 * The Python script. Reads Superset terminal-identity env vars set by
 * the terminal launcher and writes
 * `~/.superset/session-pane-map/<sessionId>.json`. Both v1 and v2
 * terminal stacks are handled — v1 sets SUPERSET_PANE_ID/TAB_ID/
 * WORKSPACE_ID (apps/desktop/src/main/lib/terminal/env.ts), v2 sets
 * SUPERSET_TERMINAL_ID/WORKSPACE_ID (packages/host-service/src/
 * terminal/env.ts). The renderer's V2NotificationController bridge
 * requires `terminalId` (not paneId), so v2 sessions must carry that
 * field through to the AGENT_LIFECYCLE event. The hook payload comes
 * from stdin (Claude / Mastra / Droid) OR argv[1] (Codex). Silent on
 * every failure path — a broken hook must not abort the agent.
 */
const PANE_MAP_SCRIPT = `#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Superset pane-map SessionStart hook (v1).

Installed by agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts. Writes a
{paneId, tabId, workspaceId} record keyed by the agent session id
so the watcher can resolve per-pane identity beyond cwd matching.

Logging: every invocation appends one JSON line to
~/.superset/pane-map-hook.log (gate with SUPERSET_AGENT_WATCHER_DEBUG=0).
The logger can never raise — a broken hook must not abort the agent.
"""
import datetime
import json
import os
import pathlib
import sys


def _log(record: dict) -> None:
    # Append one JSON line to ~/.superset/pane-map-hook.log. Fully
    # self-contained and never raises: any failure (disk, perms,
    # serialization) is swallowed so the hook can never break the agent.
    if os.environ.get("SUPERSET_AGENT_WATCHER_DEBUG") == "0":
        return
    try:
        record["ts"] = datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()
        record["phase"] = "hook"
        log_dir = pathlib.Path.home() / ".superset"
        log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        log_path = log_dir / "pane-map-hook.log"
        with open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(record) + "\\n")
    except Exception:
        pass


def _read_payload():
    # Codex passes the hook payload as argv[1]; Claude/Mastra/Droid
    # pipe via stdin. Try both. Returns (payload_or_None, source,
    # skip_reason). source is "argv[1]" | "stdin" | "none". skip_reason
    # distinguishes invalid-payload-json vs payload-not-object for the
    # diagnostic log; main() decides whether to abort.
    stdin_bytes = 0
    candidates = []
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        candidates.append(("argv[1]", sys.argv[1]))
    try:
        # (HOOK-STDIN-UTF8) Hook payloads are UTF-8, but text-mode stdin on
        # Windows decodes with the locale code page (cp1252): any non-ASCII
        # payload char mojibakes and downstream string matching silently
        # fails. Always decode the raw bytes as UTF-8.
        raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
        if raw:
            stdin_bytes = len(raw.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
            candidates.append(("stdin", raw))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    if not candidates:
        return None, "none", "none", stdin_bytes
    saw_parse_error = False
    for source, src in candidates:
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(src)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            saw_parse_error = True
            continue
        if isinstance(parsed, dict):
            return parsed, source, None, stdin_bytes
        return None, source, "payload-not-object", stdin_bytes
    return None, candidates[0][0], "invalid-payload-json" if saw_parse_error else "none", stdin_bytes


def main() -> None:
    pid = os.getpid()
    argv_count = len(sys.argv)
    superset_env = {
        "SUPERSET_PANE_ID": os.environ.get("SUPERSET_PANE_ID", ""),
        "SUPERSET_TAB_ID": os.environ.get("SUPERSET_TAB_ID", ""),
        "SUPERSET_TERMINAL_ID": os.environ.get("SUPERSET_TERMINAL_ID", ""),
        "SUPERSET_WORKSPACE_ID": os.environ.get("SUPERSET_WORKSPACE_ID", ""),
    }

    # Read both v1 and v2 terminal-identity env vars. At least one of
    # pane_id (v1) or terminal_id (v2) must be present to indicate this
    # is a Superset-launched terminal.
    pane_id = os.environ.get("SUPERSET_PANE_ID", "").strip()
    tab_id = os.environ.get("SUPERSET_TAB_ID", "").strip()
    terminal_id = os.environ.get("SUPERSET_TERMINAL_ID", "").strip()
    workspace_id = os.environ.get("SUPERSET_WORKSPACE_ID", "").strip()
    if not pane_id and not terminal_id:
        _log({
            "pid": pid,
            "argvCount": argv_count,
            "stdinBytes": 0,
            "payloadSource": "none",
            "payloadKeys": [],
            "rawSessionIdFields": {},
            "sessionId": None,
            "supersetEnv": superset_env,
            "mapping": None,
            "action": "skip",
            "skipReason": "missing-terminal-env",
            "outPath": None,
            "error": None,
        })
        return  # not inside a Superset-launched terminal

    payload, payload_source, payload_skip, stdin_bytes = _read_payload()
    payload_dict = payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}
    payload_keys = sorted(payload_dict.keys())
    raw_session_id_fields = {
        "session_id": payload_dict.get("session_id"),
        "sessionId": payload_dict.get("sessionId"),
        "resourceId": payload_dict.get("resourceId"),
        "resource_id": payload_dict.get("resource_id"),
    }
    if payload_skip in ("invalid-payload-json", "payload-not-object"):
        _log({
            "pid": pid,
            "argvCount": argv_count,
            "stdinBytes": stdin_bytes,
            "payloadSource": payload_source,
            "payloadKeys": payload_keys,
            "rawSessionIdFields": raw_session_id_fields,
            "sessionId": None,
            "supersetEnv": superset_env,
            "mapping": None,
            "action": "skip",
            "skipReason": payload_skip,
            "outPath": None,
            "error": None,
        })
        return

    session_id = (
        payload_dict.get("session_id")
        or payload_dict.get("sessionId")
        or payload_dict.get("resourceId")
        or payload_dict.get("resource_id")
    )
    if not session_id or not isinstance(session_id, str):
        _log({
            "pid": pid,
            "argvCount": argv_count,
            "stdinBytes": stdin_bytes,
            "payloadSource": payload_source,
            "payloadKeys": payload_keys,
            "rawSessionIdFields": raw_session_id_fields,
            "sessionId": session_id if isinstance(session_id, str) else None,
            "supersetEnv": superset_env,
            "mapping": None,
            "action": "skip",
            "skipReason": "missing-session-id",
            "outPath": None,
            "error": None,
        })
        return

    # Only emit fields that have values — keeps the mapping file
    # minimal and lets the watcher's spread skip undefined fields.
    mapping: dict = {}
    if pane_id:
        mapping["paneId"] = pane_id
    if tab_id:
        mapping["tabId"] = tab_id
    if terminal_id:
        mapping["terminalId"] = terminal_id
    if workspace_id:
        mapping["workspaceId"] = workspace_id

    out_dir = pathlib.Path.home() / ".superset" / "session-pane-map"
    try:
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    except OSError as exc:
        _log({
            "pid": pid,
            "argvCount": argv_count,
            "stdinBytes": stdin_bytes,
            "payloadSource": payload_source,
            "payloadKeys": payload_keys,
            "rawSessionIdFields": raw_session_id_fields,
            "sessionId": session_id,
            "supersetEnv": superset_env,
            "mapping": mapping,
            "action": "skip",
            "skipReason": "mkdir-failed",
            "outPath": None,
            "error": str(exc),
        })
        return
    out_path = out_dir / f"{session_id}.json"
    try:
        out_path.write_text(
            json.dumps(mapping),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
    except OSError as exc:
        _log({
            "pid": pid,
            "argvCount": argv_count,
            "stdinBytes": stdin_bytes,
            "payloadSource": payload_source,
            "payloadKeys": payload_keys,
            "rawSessionIdFields": raw_session_id_fields,
            "sessionId": session_id,
            "supersetEnv": superset_env,
            "mapping": mapping,
            "action": "skip",
            "skipReason": "write-failed",
            "outPath": str(out_path),
            "error": str(exc),
        })
        return

    _log({
        "pid": pid,
        "argvCount": argv_count,
        "stdinBytes": stdin_bytes,
        "payloadSource": payload_source,
        "payloadKeys": payload_keys,
        "rawSessionIdFields": raw_session_id_fields,
        "sessionId": session_id,
        "supersetEnv": superset_env,
        "mapping": mapping,
        "action": "write",
        "skipReason": None,
        "outPath": str(out_path),
        "error": None,
    })


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
`;

import base64
import collections
import datetime
import errno
import json
import os
import pathlib
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request


_ROTATED = set()


def _rotate(log_path, backup_path):
    # Roll <log> to <log>.1 once it passes ~1MB, keeping exactly ONE backup.
    # Shared by _log and _decision_log, which rotate identically.
    #
    # Path.replace, not rename: it overwrites an existing backup (rename raises
    # on Windows when the target exists), so the old exists/unlink dance is
    # gone and a second rotation REPLACES the backup instead of failing.
    #
    # Checked once per process per path. A hook process is short-lived and
    # writes well under 10KB, so it cannot cross the 1MB line mid-run; stat()ing
    # on every _log call only re-answered the same question. Best-effort: any
    # failure leaves the log where it is. Never raises.
    key = str(log_path)
    if key in _ROTATED:
        return
    _ROTATED.add(key)
    try:
        if log_path.stat().st_size > 1048576:
            log_path.replace(backup_path)
    except Exception:
        pass


def _log(record):
    # Append one JSON line to ~/.superset/agent-notify-hook.log. Never raises.
    #
    # Rotates at ~1MB with a single .log.1 backup (see _rotate). This runs on
    # EVERY hook event (not just terminal decisions), so without rotation it
    # grows without bound: a live install reached 508MB.
    if os.environ.get("SUPERSET_AGENT_WATCHER_DEBUG") == "0":
        return
    try:
        record["ts"] = datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()
        log_dir = pathlib.Path.home() / ".superset"
        log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        log_path = log_dir / "agent-notify-hook.log"
        _rotate(log_path, log_dir / "agent-notify-hook.log.1")
        with open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as h:
            h.write(json.dumps(record) + "\\n")
    except Exception:
        pass


def _decision_log(terminal_id, session_id, event_type, reason):
    # ALWAYS-ON (independent of SUPERSET_AGENT_WATCHER_DEBUG) one-line audit of a
    # terminal turn-end dot decision, so a stuck dot can be diagnosed after the
    # fact without reproducing it. Written ONLY at terminal decisions (Stop /
    # SubagentStop / StopFailure / manual-compact finish) — NOT on every
    # PostToolUse — so it stays cheap and bounded. Rotates at ~1MB via the
    # shared _rotate (single .log.1 backup, checked once per process -- a
    # process writes at most a handful of these lines).
    # Best-effort: ANY failure here is swallowed so the hook
    # still POSTs even if logging breaks. Never raises.
    try:
        ts = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
        log_dir = pathlib.Path.home() / ".superset" / "logs"
        log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        log_path = log_dir / "dot-decisions.log"
        _rotate(log_path, log_dir / "dot-decisions.log.1")
        line = (
            ts
            + " terminal=" + str(terminal_id)
            + " session=" + str(session_id)
            + " eventType=" + str(event_type)
            + " " + str(reason)
        )
        with open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as h:
            h.write(line + "\\n")
    except Exception:
        pass


def _read_payload():
    candidates = []
    try:
        # (HOOK-STDIN-UTF8) UTF-8-decode the raw bytes: Windows text-mode
        # stdin decodes cp1252 and mojibakes non-ASCII payload chars. Captured
        # live 2026-07-28: a teammate background_tasks description's em-dash
        # (U+2014, 3 UTF-8 bytes) arrived as 3 cp1252 chars, so the
        # (TEAM-ENTRY-MATCH) prefix match against the correctly-decoded
        # transcript prompt failed on that one entry forever -> the lead
        # terminal's dot latched yellow with zero agents running. Strict
        # decode first (payloads are harness-emitted JSON, always valid
        # UTF-8); on the never-expected failure, log loud and fall back to
        # replacement decoding so the hook still POSTs the lifecycle event.
        data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
        try:
            raw = data.decode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
            try:
                _log({
                    "action": "payload-decode-error",
                    "error": str(exc),
                    "stdinBytes": len(data),
                })
            except Exception:
                pass
            raw = data.decode("utf-8", "replace")
        if raw:
            candidates.append(raw)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        candidates.append(sys.argv[1])
    for src in candidates:
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(src)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            continue
        if isinstance(parsed, dict):
            return parsed
    return {}


def _subagent_dir(terminal_id):
    return pathlib.Path.home() / ".superset" / "agent-subagent-running" / terminal_id


def _sentinel_path(terminal_id):
    return (
        pathlib.Path.home()
        / ".superset"
        / "agent-subagent-running"
        / (terminal_id + ".mainstopped")
    )


def _compact_marker_path(terminal_id):
    # (COMPACT-YELLOW) records "a compaction is running" plus its trigger
    # (manual|auto) so the finish path knows how to clear the dot.

        pathlib.Path.home()
        / ".superset"
        / "agent-subagent-running"
        / (terminal_id + ".compacting")
    )


def _agentbg_marker_path(terminal_id):
    # (TEAM-YELLOW) records "the latest Stop/SubagentStop snapshot saw
    # agent-type background work still running". Consumed by the manual-compact
    # finish path, whose SessionStart payload carries NO background_tasks of
    # its own — without it, /compact ending while teammates/workflows run
    # would false-green. Refreshed from every turn-end payload; a stale marker
    # errs yellow (safe) and clears at the next bg-free turn end.
    return (
        pathlib.Path.home()
        / ".superset"
        / "agent-subagent-running"
        / (terminal_id + ".agentbg")
    )


def _shellbg_marker_path(terminal_id):
    # Sibling of .agentbg for the BLUE direction: records "the latest
    # Stop/SubagentStop snapshot saw ONLY shell-type background work still
    # running". Consumed by the same manual-compact finish path so /compact
    # ending while a background shell runs restores the BackgroundRunning
    # blue instead of false-greening (verified live 2026-06-11). A stale
    # marker errs blue-lingers — the same accepted (BA)/(BE) tradeoff — and
    # clears at the next turn end.
    return (
        pathlib.Path.home()
        / ".superset"
        / "agent-subagent-running"
        / (terminal_id + ".shellbg")
    )


def _bgactive_marker_path(terminal_id):
    # (BG-STALE) Last time REAL teammate/subagent activity was seen for this
    # terminal (a SubagentStart or a subagent-scoped PostToolUse). Consulted at a
    # turn-end agent-hold: an agent set Claude Code still reports "running" but
    # that has produced no activity for _BG_STALE_SECONDS is idle/zombie and must
    # stop pinning the lead's dot yellow (the harness never flips an idle
    # long-lived teammate, or one that died without a clean SubagentStop, to a
    # finished status). Refreshed ONLY on genuine forward activity (never on the
    # hold itself, which would keep it perpetually fresh); the JSONL watcher
    # re-asserts yellow within its poll if a reaped set turns out to still write.
    return (
        pathlib.Path.home()
        / ".superset"
        / "agent-subagent-running"
        / (terminal_id + ".bgactive")
    )


def _pending_failure_path(terminal_id):
    # (DEFERRED-FAILURE) records "a MAIN-loop StopFailure was DEFERRED because a
    # codex companion was still working". The abort is real, but announcing it
    # immediately would drop the companion's yellow hold, so the Failed dot is
    # parked here and released by the FIRST later turn-end that finds no hold
    # left — a Stop, the companion's own SubagentStop, or a later StopFailure.
    # EVERY one of those emits Failed instead of green, so an abort is never
    # swallowed by the cycle that carried it. ONLY a new prompt supersedes it
    # (UserPromptSubmit — typed or an auto-resume re-send), which is what stops
    # a LATER successful turn from being marked Failed; a fresh session /
    # SessionEnd also drop it as lifecycle boundaries. Consumed exactly once,
    # wherever it is released.
    return (
        pathlib.Path.home()
        / ".superset"
        / "agent-subagent-running"
        / (terminal_id + ".pendingfailure")
    )


def _teamstate_path(terminal_id):
    # (TEAMMATE-IDLE) incremental parse cache for the lead transcript's
    # teammate ledger plus named-fork tool-use mapping. Versioned so a schema
    # change forces a full reparse and heals entries written by older code.
    # Keyed by transcript path, so a /resume (new transcript file) or terminalId
    # reuse also self-invalidates. Corruption tolerated: any read failure falls
    # back to offset 0 — self-healing, never trusted blindly.
    return (
        pathlib.Path.home()
        / ".superset"
        / "agent-subagent-running"
        / (terminal_id + ".teamstate.json")
    )


def _askq_dir(terminal_id):
    # (UNTAGGED-BG-RED) a DIRECTORY of per-owner "an AskUserQuestion is pending"
    # markers for this terminal — one file per owner (the raising agent). An
    # AskUserQuestion red's ONLY valid clear is its own answer
    # (PostToolUse:AskUserQuestion) or that owner's turn boundary — NEVER a
    # generic main-loop tool completion. While ANY marker exists an untagged
    # ordinary PostToolUse asserts working WITHOUT clearing the red, so a
